events.title: Demo v1.4.022 - Some changes around the shop
events.summary: Hey everyone, I ended up changing quite a bit for this update. Some criticism about the game looking unoriginal because of the Synty characters got to me, and honestly, I took it personally. That pushed me to spend more time on the game's appearance. I'm still learning, and I don't think replacing some models suddenly solves everything. But it gave me a reason to revisit the customers, the shop and the apartment, along with some things that were confusing or just weren't working properly. Custom

events.title: v1.4.020 - the freezes were my fault, and here's what they were
events.summary: Some of you got a game that froze at the logo, or showed the main menu and then locked up on the loading screen, or ran at one frame every ten seconds. One review called it horrible. That was a fair word for what you got, and this update is mostly about it. What was actually happening The game ships its shaders pre-compiled so your graphics card doesn't have to do that work the first time the store draws. Except it didn't. events.title: A better day behind the counter
events.summary: Hi everyone, I've been working through your recordings and reports. This Demo and Playtest update catches up on the changes since September 6, including fixes that reached the builds between posts. Quick highlights A new first-era computer look, inspired by Windows 2000/XP, with clearer orders and budgets. Better trade-ins and repairs, from grading a copy to opening the Nexus cartridge and using the tools. More natural hands and customers, with improved shelf pickups, basket unloading and paymen

events.summary: Hey everyone! Last time I posted here was in August, before the demo was out. events.title: Big Update: 823 changes since this page went up - play it free right now
events.summary: I've been busyWhen this page went up in April I was just one person, building a game store sim with no budget, and that you could come and watch me build it. Since then there have been 823 changes to the game. Almost all of it landed in the playtest, which is free and open to everyone right now. events.title: We Just Went Live on Steam. The Journey Starts Here.
events.summary: We have a Steam page! This is real now.I'm not here to announce a launch. The game isn't ready for that yet. But the Steam page is live, and that feels like a milestone worth sharing.I'm one person. I started with zero game dev experience. No team, no studio, no budget. Just an idea I couldn't shake: what if you could run your own game store, starting in the late '90s, and live through every console generation?So I started building it.What's already working🎮 Hands-on retail - Stock shelves, scan
